original_question: Let M be the one-dimensional centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, and let BV(R) denote the Banach space of functions f : R -> R of bounded total variation with norm ||f||_{BV(R)} = |f(-infinity)| + Var(f). Is the map M : BV(R) -> BV(R) continuous?
target_in_paper: Section 7.1, Question 14: the continuity problem for the one-dimensional centered classical Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator on the normalized BV(ℝ) Banach space. This is the exact open problem your draft is aiming at. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
correct_elements: Your draft already has the right operator, the right ambient space, the right normed BV setting, and the right property: it asks about the continuous one-dimensional centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator acting on BV(ℝ) with the normalized norm |f(-∞)|+Var(f). That matches Question 14, not the neighboring centered W^{1,1} question (Question 12) or the uncentered BV question (Question 13). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
missing_details: Write M explicitly, e.g. M f(x)=sup_{r>0}(1/(2r))∫_{x-r}^{x+r}|f(y)|dy, so the problem is unmistakably about the centered classical maximal operator from equation (1.1), not an uncentered, discrete, or fractional variant. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))

State continuity in norm-topological terms: if f_j→f in the normalized BV(ℝ) norm, then M f_j→M f in the same norm. The paper poses the question exactly at that level of Banach-space continuity. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
Keep explicit that the BV norm is the normalized Banach norm with the extra |f(-∞)| term. That is the framework in which Question 14 is posed. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
Say that functions are real-valued, matching the standing convention of the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
refined_question: Let M be the centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator on ℝ, M f(x)=sup_{r>0}(1/(2r))∫_{x-r}^{x+r}|f(y)|dy. Let BV(ℝ) be the Banach space of real-valued functions of bounded total variation equipped with the normalized norm ||f||_BV := |f(-∞)| + Var(f). Is M continuous as a map BV(ℝ)→BV(ℝ); equivalently, does ||f_j-f||_BV→0 imply ||M f_j-M f||_BV→0? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
justification: The nearest official formulation in arXiv:1912.04625 is Question 14 in Section 7.1, posed immediately after the paper recalls that the centered maximal operator is already bounded on BV through Kurka’s variation estimate (Theorem 3.2 / (3.4)) and after it fixes the normalized BV Banach norm. So the paper-faithful question is not a broader BV-regularity problem, nor the neighboring centered W^{1,1} continuity problem (Question 12), nor the uncentered BV problem (Question 13); it is precisely the centered classical BV-continuity question on ℝ. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1912.04625))
